fullPassage:
Vision is our dominant sense, and you want to look both ways before crossing the street — it’s the first thing parents drill into their children. But that doesn’t mean our sense of hearing isn’t a big deal. I don’t have to mention the worn-out example of cavemen and hidden saber-toothed tigers. There’s something that can sneak up and kill you today: a silent electric car. These pose an unanticipated but serious threat to pedestrians and bicyclists, who depend on engine noise to detect and orient to cars — so much so that the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration now requires slow-moving electric vehicles to generate a warning noise. It’s a reminder that even for us in a modern city, having both cues can mean the difference between life and death.

Sometimes traditions may change or appear to end because of convenience or changes in taste. For example, to make a pumpkin pie, a cook used to have to first find a pumpkin of suitable size, cut it, peel it, cook it, and mash it, all before combining it with other ingredients and pouring the mixture into a crust. Now, cooks may choose to use canned pumpkin from the supermarket and cut out a great deal of labor and time. Another changing food tradition is that many families no longer make refried beans by cooking them in lard and choose instead to use vegetable shortening. Perhaps this change came about because the family has come to prefer the taste of beans without lard, because concepts of healthy cooking have changed, or because someone in the family has heart disease or high cholesterol.

Forecasters who predict resource depletion often ignore or underestimate the power of markets. For example, some forecasters use a current reserve index to estimate how long a resource would last. The current reserve index divides the current known reserve of a resource by the amount currently used each period. So, if we know of 445 billion barrels of oil, and we are currently using 15 billion barrels per year, the index indicates that we will run out of oil in about 30 years. Some studies, like the Limits to Growth, further assume that demand will increase each year, thus depleting resources even faster. But what they fail to see is that if markets are allowed to do their usual duty, that is, prices rise as depletion occurs, resources will last much longer.

Project leaders should not be surprised when disagreements emerge within the team. In fact, they should expect them. If they remain hidden, the leader may even want to seek them out for at least two reasons. First, different views can bring with them good ideas about the project and how it might be run. Although snap decisions about project changes should be avoided, leaders should be open to new and better ways to run the project. Second, when conflicting viewpoints are found, they are more easily resolved earlier rather than later in the project. Although team members may disagree about one or another aspect of the project, most simply want their ideas considered and resolved. The team tends to look to the project leader to play the lead role in resolving differences, and members will generally defer to the leader if they believe their views have been given due consideration.

questions.passage:
Vision is our dominant sense, and you want to look both ways before crossing the street — it’s the first thing parents drill into their children. But that doesn’t mean our sense of hearing isn’t a big deal. I don’t have to mention the worn-out example of cavemen and hidden saber-toothed tigers. There’s something that can sneak up and kill you today: a silent electric car. These pose an unanticipated but serious threat to pedestrians and bicyclists, who depend on engine noise to detect and orient to cars — so much so that the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration now requires slow-moving electric vehicles to generate a warning noise. It’s a reminder that even for us in a modern city, having both cues can mean the difference between life and death.

Sometimes traditions may change or appear to end because of convenience or changes in taste. For example, to make a pumpkin pie, a cook used to have to first find a pumpkin of suitable size, cut it, peel it, cook it, and mash it, all before combining it with other ingredients and pouring the mixture into a crust. Now, cooks may choose to use canned pumpkin from the supermarket and cut out a great deal of labor and time. Another changing food tradition is that many families no longer make refried beans by cooking them in lard and choose instead to use vegetable shortening. Perhaps this change came about because the family has come to prefer the taste of beans without lard, because concepts of healthy cooking have changed, or because someone in the family has heart disease or high cholesterol.

Forecasters who predict resource depletion often ignore or underestimate the power of markets. For example, some forecasters use a current reserve index to __________ how long a resource would last. The current reserve index divides the current known reserve of a resource by the amount currently used each period. So, if we know of 445 billion barrels of oil, and we are currently using 15 billion barrels per year, the index indicates that we will run out of oil in about 30 years. Some studies, like the Limits to Growth, further assume that demand will increase each year, thus depleting resources even faster. But what they fail to see is that if markets are allowed to do their usual duty, that is, prices rise as depletion occurs, resources will last much longer.

Project leaders should not be surprised when disagreements emerge within the team. In fact, they should expect them. If they remain hidden, the leader may even want to seek them out for at least two reasons. First, different views can bring with them good ideas about the project and how it might be run. Although snap decisions about project changes should be avoided, leaders should be open to new and better ways to run the project. Second, when conflicting viewpoints are found, they are more easily resolved earlier rather than later in the project. Although team members may disagree about one or another aspect of the project, most simply want their ideas considered and resolved. The team tends to look to the project leader to play the lead role in resolving differences, and members will generally defer to the leader if they believe their views have been given due consideration.

questions.passage:

(B) I'd like to <u>reserve</u> a table for four at 7 p.m. this Friday evening, please.
questions.stem: 다음 (A)와 (B)의 밑줄 친 reserve의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) reserve = 매장량, 비축량 / (B) reserve = 예약하다
det.analysis:
❌ ① (A) 예약 — (B) 매장량: (A)는 자원의 매장량, 예약이 아님
✅ ② (A) 매장량 — (B) 예약하다: (A)는 자원 매장량 지수, (B)는 테이블 예약 ←정답
❌ ③ (A) 보유량 — (B) 보존하다: (B)는 예약하다이지 보존이 아님
❌ ④ (A) 예약 — (B) 예약하다: (A)는 매장량 지수의 맥락

det.analysis:
✅ ① sneak(몰래 다가가다): 조용히 비밀리에 접근 — 정의 일치 ←정답
❌ ② detect(감지하다): 발견하는 것이지 접근하는 것이 아님
❌ ③ generate(발생시키다): 만들어내는 것이지 접근이 아님
❌ ④ emerge(나타나다): 드러나는 것이지 몰래 접근이 아님
det.tip: sneak = creep, steal (몰래 다가가다, 살금살금 가다)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: by + 동명사: ~함으로써. cook → cooking
det.analysis: 전치사 by 뒤에는 동명사(V-ing)가 온다. cook(동사원형) → cooking(동명사)으로 어형 변환. 'by cooking them in lard' = 라드에 요리함으로써

questions.passage: Second, when conflicting viewpoints are found, they are more __________ (easy) resolved earlier rather than later in the project.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: easy(형용사) → easily(부사): resolved(과거분사)를 수식하는 부사 필요
det.analysis: 과거분사 resolved를 수식하려면 부사가 필요. easy(형용사: 쉬운) → easily(부사: 쉽게)로 어형 변환. 'more easily resolved' = 더 쉽게 해결된
det.tip: easy(adj. 쉬운) → easily(adv. 쉽게). 비교급: more easily

questions.passage:
Vision is our dominant sense, and you want to look both ways before crossing the street — it’s the first thing parents drill into their children. But that doesn’t mean our sense of hearing isn’t a big deal. I don’t have to mention the worn-out example of cavemen and hidden saber-toothed tigers. There’s something that can sneak up and kill you today: a silent electric car. These pose an unanticipated but serious threat to pedestrians and bicyclists, who depend on engine noise to detect and orient to cars — so much so that the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration now requires slow-moving electric vehicles to generate a warning noise. It’s a reminder that even for us in a modern city, having both cues can mean __________.

Sometimes traditions may change or appear to end because of convenience or changes in taste. For example, to make a pumpkin pie, a cook used to have to first find a pumpkin of suitable size, cut it, peel it, cook it, and mash it, all before combining it with other ingredients and pouring the mixture into a crust. Now, cooks may choose to use canned pumpkin from the supermarket and cut out a great deal of labor and time. Another changing food tradition is that many families no longer make refried beans by cooking them in lard and choose instead to use vegetable shortening. Perhaps this change came about because the family has come to prefer the taste of beans without lard, because concepts of healthy cooking have changed, or because someone in the family has heart disease or high cholesterol.

Forecasters who predict resource depletion often ignore or underestimate the power of markets. For example, some forecasters use a current reserve index to estimate how long a resource would last. The current reserve index divides the current known reserve of a resource by the amount currently used each period. So, if we know of 445 billion barrels of oil, and we are currently using 15 billion barrels per year, the index indicates that we will run out of oil in about 30 years. Some studies, like the Limits to Growth, further assume that demand will increase each year, thus depleting resources even faster. But what they fail to see is that if markets are allowed to do their usual duty, that is, prices rise as depletion occurs, resources will last much longer.

Project leaders should not be surprised when disagreements emerge within the team. In fact, they should expect them. If they remain hidden, the leader may even want to seek them out for at least two reasons. First, different views can bring with them good ideas about the project and how it might be run. Although snap decisions about project changes should be avoided, leaders should be open to new and better ways to run the project. Second, when conflicting viewpoints are found, they are more easily resolved earlier rather than later in the project. Although team members may disagree about one or another aspect of the project, most simply want their ideas considered and resolved. The team tends to look to the project leader to play the lead role in resolving differences, and members will generally defer to the leader if they believe their views have been given due consideration.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 두 감각(시각+청각)을 모두 가지는 것이 삶과 죽음의 차이를 의미할 수 있다
det.analysis:
❌ ① a minor inconvenience(사소한 불편): 삶과 죽음의 맥락에서 너무 약한 표현
❌ ② a source of entertainment(오락 거리): 전기차 위험의 맥락과 무관
✅ ③ the difference between life and death(삶과 죽음의 차이): 두 단서를 모두 가지는 것이 생사의 차이 — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ④ an unnecessary expense(불필요한 비용): 감각의 맥락에서 비용은 무관
det.tip: the difference between life and death = 생사의 갈림길, 삶과 죽음의 차이

ch: the difference between life and death

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 시장이 제 역할을 하면, 즉 고갈이 발생함에 따라 가격이 오르면 자원이 훨씬 오래 지속된다
det.analysis:
❌ ① governments impose strict regulations(정부가 엄격한 규제를 부과): 시장의 역할이지 정부 규제가 아님
❌ ② consumers voluntarily reduce demand(소비자가 자발적으로 수요를 줄임): 시장 메커니즘(가격)이지 자발적 감소가 아님
❌ ③ new technologies replace old resources(새 기술이 오래된 자원을 대체): 시장 가격 메커니즘과 다른 주제
✅ ④ prices rise as depletion occurs(고갈이 발생하면 가격이 오른다): 시장의 통상적 역할 — 원문 일치 ←정답
det.tip: 시장 메커니즘: 자원 희소 → 가격 상승 → 소비 감소 → 자원 수명 연장
